title: How does a caller get a FASTA record's sequence into a buffer it owns?
body:
`FastaParser::parse(bytes) -> Result<FastaRecord>` in `seq/fasta.rs` is the one function that drops the line breaks from a FASTA record's residues. It writes them into a new `Vec` in `FastaRecord::seq`, reserved at the residues' length. A caller that gathers many records into one buffer copies every residue twice and allocates once per record.

sufr does that. Its `read_sequence_file` joins every record of its input into one text, with a delimiter byte between records. On a 3.1 GB genome the extra copy is 3.1 GB, and peak memory grows by the largest record.

## Options

- An append. `fasta::append_seq(record: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>)` adds the record's residues, without whitespace, to the end of `out`. It suits a caller that joins records, and it pairs with `name_of`, which already reads a name without parsing.
- A parse into a reused record. `FastaParser::parse_into(record: &[u8], out: &mut FastaRecord)` clears `out` and refills `name`, `extra` and `seq`. It suits a caller that handles one record at a time. A caller that joins records still copies once out of `seq`.

Either one is new API beside `parse` and changes nothing that exists.

I lean to the append. The caller behind this issue is sufr, and `parse_into` would save sufr the allocation but not the copy.

## Open

- Which of the two, or both.
- sufr is timing libsail's `index::Reader` against needletail, with `parse` as it is (sufr-409cc8). If sufr switches to libsail, it needs this soon.
